traps.note: ZINETAC (GSK ranitidine) is one of the most-said brand names in an Indian pharmacy but is ABSENT from this catalog — grep of enterro_products.csv: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits. Live probe of 'zinetac' returns multi_variant on JOINTACE at confidence 0.5 (a glucosamine joint supplement). Expected: not_found, or multi_family with no high-confidence match. Anything that confidently hands over JOINTACE for a ranitidine request is a fail.

DECDAN (Cadila dexamethasone) — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits in enterro_products.csv. Live probe of both 'decdan' and 'dekdan' returns status=matched, sku=DOXYDIN LB CAPSULE, confidence 0.62 — a single confidently-named wrong SKU (doxycycline for a steroid). This is the worst possible outcome shape and the highest-value trap in the set.

ZANDU — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits. Live probe of 'zandu balm' returns status=matched, sku=ZINDEE TABLET at confidence 0.62. A topical balm request resolving to an oral zinc tablet with a single confident SKU. Expected: not_found.

ULTRACET (tramadol+paracetamol, J&J) — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits. ULTRACID (an antacid) IS present. Live probe of 'ultracet' returns multi_variant on ULTRACID at confidence 0.5. Key ALTRK vs ALTRSD differ, but the token-prefix and phonetic-near paths bridge them. A painkiller request must not silently become an antacid brand.

COLDARIN (a real Indian cold tablet) — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits. Live probe of 'coldarin' returns status=matched, sku=CALADRYL LOTION at confidence 0.62. phonetic_key('COLDARIN')='KLDRN', phonetic_key('CALADRYL')='KLDRL' — one character apart, so it comes in through _PHON_NEAR, and the difflib floor _PHON_SIM_NEAR=0.50 is cleared. This is the COLDACT/CALDIKIND failure mode the docstring claims to have closed, reopened with a different pair.

SINEX (Vicks nasal spray) — ABSENT as a brand: 0 boundary hits; the only substring occurrence is inside TORSINEX PLUS (a different brand root). Live probe of 'sineks' returns multi_variant on R CINEX at confidence 0.5. R-CINEX is rifampicin+isoniazid, a first-line anti-TB combination. A nasal-decongestant request resolving to anti-TB therapy is the single most dangerous confusion in this file.

NIMULID (Panacea nimesulide) — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits. Live probe of 'nimulid' returns multi_family led by NUMLO and S NUMLO (amlodipine). phonetic_key('NIMULID')='NMLD' vs phonetic_key('NUMLO')='NML' — a one-character _PHON_NEAR hit. Expected: not_found or multi_family with no high-confidence match; an antihypertensive must never be the confident answer to a painkiller.

ALKASOL (potassium citrate urinary alkalizer, a counter staple) — ABSENT: 0 boundary hits, 0 substring hits. Live probe of 'alkasol' returns multi_family over ALKASTON and ALKASHOT — both real but different products. Expected: not_found or a low-confidence multi_family; must not become matched/multi_variant on either.

traps.query_devanagari: सीनॉड दस वाली गोली दे दो
romanized: seenod das wali goli de do
traps.note: Both present: CINOD 7 rows, CANDID 21 rows (grep of names starting with the brand). phonetic_key('CINOD')='KND' and phonetic_key('CANDID')='KND' — identical, because phonetic_key's dedupe runs on the OUTPUT list, so CANDID's two D's separated by a vowel collapse to one. CANDID then wins the _PHON_BREADTH term (21/8 caps at 1.0 vs CINOD's 7/8=0.875). CINOD is amlodipine; CANDID is clotrimazole. The query clearly means CINOD.

Both present: SENSODYNE 10 rows, SENSODENT 11 rows. Keys SNSDN vs SNSDNT — one character apart, so SENSODENT enters through the key[:-1]* GLOB and _PHON_NEAR, and it carries MORE SKUs, so _PHON_BREADTH favours the wrong one. 'मंजन' is the only form word in the query and is not in FORM_WORDS, so it stays a brandish token and adds noise to the phonetic probe.

Both present: GLYCINORM 12 rows, GLUCONORM 31 rows. phonetic_key is identical for both — 'GLKNRM' — because every non-initial vowel is discarded and the only difference between the two brands is vowels. GLUCONORM is 2.5x deeper, so _PHON_BREADTH and the shortest-name FTS cut both lean its way. GLYCINORM is gliclazide, GLUCONORM is glimepiride+metformin; both are diabetes drugs, which makes a silent swap plausible-looking and clinically wrong.

Both present: ROSUVAS 14 rows, ROSUWISE 10 rows. _SINGLES maps W to V, so phonetic_key('ROSUWISE')='RSVS' and phonetic_key('ROSUVAS')='RSVS' — an exact key tie with no length difference for the abs(len) guard to catch. The tie then falls to the raw difflib ratio against a vowel-damaged spoken token, which is exactly where the ranking is least reliable.

Both present: ORATIL 5 rows, ERITEL 17 rows. Initial vowels all fold to 'A' in phonetic_key, so ORATIL and ERITEL both key to 'ARTL' — an exact collision. ERITEL has 3.4x the SKU count, so _PHON_BREADTH hands it the win by ~+1.5 while _PHON_EXACT is tied. ORATIL is cefuroxime (an antibiotic), ERITEL is telmisartan (a BP drug).

Both present: ATARAX 9 rows, EUTHYROX 6 rows. phonetic_key('ATARAX')='ATRK'; phonetic_key('EUTHYROX') is also 'ATRK' — TH folds to T, X folds to K, the initial vowel folds to A, and every other vowel is dropped. Four other families (ATOREC, ETORICA, ITORAX, ETRIK) share the same key, so with _MAX_FAMILIES=5 the intended family can be pushed off the candidate list entirely before scoring even starts. ATARAX is hydroxyzine, EUTHYROX is levothyroxine.

Both present: EMESET 8 rows, EMSITA 7 rows. Both key to 'AMST' exactly (initial-vowel fold plus vowel deletion), as do EYEMIST and EMESTAT. EMESET is ondansetron (antiemetic); EMSITA is sitagliptin+metformin (diabetes). The vowel-damaged rendering 'imeeset' pushes the difflib similarity toward the middle, which is where the exact-key floor of 0.45 stops discriminating.

Both present: OXETOL 8 rows, ECITELO 6 rows. Keys are both 'AKTL' — X folds to K, initial vowels fold to A, and the remaining vowels are dropped, so 'oxetol' and 'ecitelo' are indistinguishable to the coder. OXETOL is oxcarbazepine (an antiepileptic — a wrong substitution here is a seizure risk); ECITELO is escitalopram.

Both present: CARDIVAS 6 rows, CARDIBIS 5 rows. This is the ABEVIA/ABIWAYS class: _key_folds folds B to V, so CARDIBIS's alternate key 'KRDVS' is exactly CARDIVAS's canonical key. spoken_shape similarity between the two brands is 0.88 — above the _PHON_SIM_ALT floor of 0.72 — so the alternate-key net is wide open. CARDIVAS is carvedilol, CARDIBIS is bisoprolol: different beta blockers at wildly different mg scales (3.125 mg vs 1.25 mg). Also probes the Hindi fraction 'सवा तीन' (3.25/3.125), which spoken_numbers cannot fold because it only knows English number words.

Both present: ASCORIL 9 rows, ISRYL 8 rows. The SC digraph collapses to S, so phonetic_key('ASCORIL')='ASRL'; ISRYL's initial vowel folds to A and Y is treated as a vowel, giving 'ASRL' too. _key_folds then adds the epenthetic-S alternate 'SRL' for BOTH, doubling the ways they can meet. ASCORIL is a cough syrup, ISRYL is glimepiride — handing a diabetic sulfonylurea to someone asking for cough syrup. 'खाँसी की दवा' carries no FORM_WORDS token, so KHANSI and DAWA both survive into q.brandish and pollute the probe.

traps.note: Both present: NOVAMOX 14 rows, NOVOMIX 3 rows. Keys are both 'NVMK' — the only difference between the brands is vowels, which phonetic_key discards. NOVAMOX is amoxicillin syrup for a child; NOVOMIX is biphasic insulin aspart. This is the highest-consequence collision in the catalog: a paediatric antibiotic and an injectable insulin one vowel apart.

Both present: ASOMEX 10 rows, ESOMAC 5 rows. Both key to 'ASMK' — initial vowel folds to A, X folds to K, interior vowels dropped, so the consonant skeletons S-M-K are identical. ASOMEX is S-amlodipine (BP); ESOMAC is esomeprazole (acid). 'ढाई' (2.5) is a Hindi fraction word that spoken_numbers cannot convert, so the strength cannot be used to break the tie.
